analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, patches and all supplied source excerpts. The changes are documentation: changelog.d/qwen-end-of-prompt-checkpoints.md:3-13 describes a deeper dense-Qwen SSD checkpoint on a 256-token grid, at least 64 tokens before prompt end and requiring 1,024 tokens of benefit; docs/architecture/inference.md:1387 (head patch) documents the new demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens factory setting. No supplied change establishes an authorization, encryption, data-exposure, billing or availability regression. Deeper cached prefixes can affect the accepted same-account TTFT oracle and encrypted artifact volume under T-041/A-001/TB-007, but these descriptions do not establish weakened tenant isolation, retention, cryptography or donation controls. The surrounding BASE text already describes authenticated cache scopes, artifact/prompt bindings, encrypted complete checkpoints, cancellation and memory ownership (inference.md:603-628, 652-667); its existing resident-cache descriptions are not introduced by this PR.
Integration must verify EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift and scheduler/capture implementation: the new boundary must preserve authenticated cacheSalt and model/layout identity, complete recurrent-state correctness, media exclusions, cancellation and transient-memory accounting, and existing SSD donation, staging, endurance, free-space and kill-switch guards. Those executable changes are not supplied in this batch, so the documented performance/output claims do not verify those contracts. No concrete finding is supported by this documentation-only evidence; implementation uncertainty remains material to the described cache behavior.
